filename: Variability in the Global Ocean Carbon Sink From 1959 to 2020 by Correcting Models With Observations.pdf
title: Variability in the Global Ocean Carbon Sink From 1959 to 2020 by Correcting Models With Observations
testbed_rationale: The study produces an observation-constrained, reconstructed global ocean pCO2 and flux product via offline XGBoost misfit correction rather than an ML-based parameterization or surrogate model for dynamical GCM integration.
pain_points: Sparsity of direct surface ocean pCO2 observations prior to the 1980s prevents training interannually varying corrections for 1959–1981.
Significant regional biases in the mean and seasonal cycles across Global Ocean Biogeochemical Models (GOBMs).
High uncertainty in riverine carbon efflux adjustments needed to convert net air-sea flux to anthropogenic flux (estimated at 0.49 ± 0.26 PgC/yr).
extraction_notes: LDEO-HPD extends the ML misfit-correction framework developed by Gloege et al. (2022). For 1982–2020, interannually varying XGBoost corrections are applied to 8 GOBMs; for 1959–1981, the 2000–2020 monthly climatology of XGBoost misfits is applied.
